title: rbac v2: enforce audit logging + KMS region pinning for service tokens
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds enforcement for audit logging on service token operations; enforces KMS region pinning for keys used by Private deployments; updates RBAC v2 policies with explicit deny rules for cross-region key use; includes migration notes for existing keys and a toggle for gradual rollout.
description: Motivation: Close gaps between RBAC v2 policy model and runtime enforcement for service tokens, ensure all service-token-driven KMS operations are logged, and prevent accidental cross-region KMS usage which violates data residency commitments. Summary of changes: 1) RBAC v2 policy updates: add new 'kms.region' constraint on role bindings, introduce explicit deny rule for attempts to use keys outside the allowed region, and update role templates for service_token and platform_agent roles. 2) Audit logging: require audit flag for service-token KMS operations; wire audit events into the existing audit service with structured payloads (actor, token_id, key_id, region, operation, request_id). 3) KMS integration: add region pinning at the KMS client level to reject requests where the key's metadata region does not match the tenant/route pin. 4) Migration and rollout: introduce a feature-flag 'rbac_v2_kms_region_enforce' (default off) with a canary rollout by org; provide a migration job to tag existing keys with region metadata and an operator playbook. Checklist: - [x] Policy schema and validation changes - [x] Runtime enforcement in kms client - [x] Audit events added and wired to audit service - [x] Unit + integration tests for positive/negative flows - [x] Docs + migration notes - [x] Feature-flagged rollout and telemetry. Testing: unit tests for policy eval and kms client added (integration-tests/security/kms_region_test.go); ran internal canary against dedicated staging org org-canary-3; CI initially failed due to linting on the audit payload serialization but was fixed in commit 3. Backwards compatibility: default feature flag is off so existing tenants are unaffected; teams can enable per-org to validate key metadata. Migration: provided migration script tools/migrations/kms_tag_keys.sh and docs/docs/security/rbac_v2_migration.md describing required steps for tagging keys and re-running compliance checks. Rollout plan: 1) enable feature for internal staging to collect telemetry 2) enable for 5 pilot customers 3) open rollout to GA once no regressions detected. Related: ENG-1287, SEC-401. Why this PR is large: touches policy schema, policy generation templates, runtime KMS client, audit plumbing, tests and docs. Timeline: ship as part of security sprint S2026-Q1.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) policy: add kms.region constraint and deny rule (rbac/policies/v2/role_definitions.yaml + schema validation), 2) kms: implement region pinning + rejection path (services/kms/region_pin.go + client changes), 3) audit: add structured audit events and serialization fix (services/audit/auditd/config.go) + tests and docs.

notes_for_release: Security: Enforce KMS region pinning and audit logging for service token KMS operations. Admins must run the provided migration to tag existing keys before enabling enforcement. Feature flag: rbac_v2_kms_region_enforce (off by default).
testing_notes: Integration test covers allowed region flow, cross-region rejection, missing-key-metadata rejection, and audit event emission. Ran canary in staging org-canary-3; telemetry shows 0.02% rejects for pilot keys which were remediated by tagging.
support_matrix: Affected deployments: Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated where customer-managed KMS is used. Hosted API uses Redwood-managed KMS and is opt-in until keys tagged.
